subject: Operational windows & service credit redlines (MSA / Order Form)
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudpoint.com>

Subject: Operational windows & credits - MSA redlines

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our markups to the MSA and the Order Form focusing on the uptime metric, maintenance windows, and the service credit schedule. High level notes:

- We redlined uptime to be a minimum of 99.97% measured monthly; suggested credits scale up to 30% for extended outages.
- We propose maintenance blackout periods (region-specific) rather than a global monthly window.
- Response times: require P1 acknowledgement within 15 minutes and resolution SLA language for root cause within 72 hours for critical incidents.

Please review the attached Cloudpoint_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx and let us know if Redwood has any non-negotiable constraints. Procurement would like an initial read by EOD Monday so they can schedule a legal review.

Regards,
Sara Kim
Sr. Contracts Manager | Cloudpoint Analytics
attachments: Cloudpoint_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudpoint.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational windows & credits - MSA redlines

Sara — thanks for sending this over. Appreciated the clear callouts. Looping in Lauren from Legal and Marissa from Sales so we can coordinate proposed counter-redlines.

Quick reactions (we'll follow with annotated PDF):
- Uptime target: Redwood's standard for this tier is 99.95% monthly. We can consider 99.97% if Cloudpoint agrees to a reduced credit slab and a 12-month ramp to the higher target.
- Credits: Redwood typically caps monthly service credits at 10% of monthly fees for non-availability, with an additional escalation gate for repeated breaches. We are open to a higher cap but will need to preserve a cap to avoid run-rate exposure.
- Maintenance windows: we prefer one scheduled maintenance window per month (up to 4 hours) with documented advance notice and region-aware opt-outs for regulated accounts. Full global blackout windows complicate routing and failovers.
- Response times: we can commit to 15 minute acknowledgement for P1s and a 4-hour engineer engagement SLA; RCA timing is negotiable but should use a 72-hour target for initial RCA and a 30-day final root-cause report for complex failures.

I'll attach an annotated version of our counterpoints (KP_annotated_redlines.pdf). Can we set a 30-minute sync early next week to walk legal through the differences?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
attachments: KP_annotated_redlines.pdf
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Legal takeaways on Cloudpoint redlines

Kimberly / team — quick internal note after my first pass on Cloudpoint_MSA_Redlines_v1: 

1) Availability measurement: They want the measurement to be from their vantage only. We should insist on dual measurement (provider + customer) with a clause that prioritizes provider logs for credit calculation, and allow customer to request audit logs if discrepancy > 0.5%.

2) Credit schedule: Their scale to 30% is disproportionate for a single-month outage; propose a tiered approach: 10% (99.9-99.95), 20% (99.5-99.9), 30% (<99.5) with an absolute cap per incident at 50% and a monthly cap at 15% during the negotiation window. This preserves contractual accountability but limits financial exposure.

3) Maintenance: A per-region maintenance opt-out is reasonable only if accompanied by explicit routing rules (i.e., requests routed to alternate region) and compensating SLO allowances. Ask ops for runbook impacts.

4) P1 ack/resolution: 15-minute ack is acceptable. For resolution, replace hard 'RCA within 72 hours' with 'initial RCA within 72 hours; final RCA within 30 days or earlier if cause isolated.'

I'll prepare a clean tracked-changes set for the Order Form and MSA. Connor — can you confirm operational impact of per-region blackout by Monday?

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: procurement@cloudpoint.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com; lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudpoint.com>, michael.hayes@cloudpoint.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational windows & credits - MSA redlines

Hi Kimberly / Lauren — appreciate the quick reply and the annotated PDF. A few clarifications from procurement/legal: 

- On maintenance: Cloudpoint insists on regional blackout windows — our security teams require the ability to pause maintenance in critical regions during key business cycles. Can Redwood propose a routing plan that guarantees traffic continuity without imposing full global freezes? If routing is workable, we can accept the monthly window but need the regional opt-out language.

- Credits: we cannot accept a 10% hard cap for severe multi-day outages. Our accounting will not approve anything less than 15% for repeated incidents, and 25% for catastrophic events. We can consider gradual reduction if you commit to N-1 regional redundancy and publish incident postmortems.

- Can we do a short technical call Tuesday 11/10 10:00 AM PT to discuss routing and failover capability? Also need confirmation that Redwood can provide raw telemetry logs for a 90-day period on request.

If you prefer, we can escalate to execs to get alignment quickly.

Regards,
Cloudpoint Procurement Team
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudpoint.com>, procurement@cloudpoint.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800

Thanks — agreed on next steps and capturing in writing so legal has a clean playbook for the redlines: 

Action items / summary:
1) Ops sync (technical): Tuesday 2026-11-10 10:00 AM PT — Connor will cover routing, N-1 redundancy, and whether per-region maintenance opt-outs can be supported without impacting SLOs.
2) Legal follow-up: Lauren will deliver a tracked-changes MSA + Order Form by EOD Wednesday 2026-11-11 reflecting: dual-measurement language, the proposed tiered credit schedule (with a negotiation cap of 15% monthly during ramp), and RCA timelines (initial 72h, final 30d).
3) Telemetry: Redwood confirms we can provide raw telemetry for 90 days on request; we'll include an audit access clause and log-extract process.
4) Finance / commercial: Marissa to model impact of credit caps (10% vs 15% vs 25%) and include a ramp proposal tied to usage milestones — Marissa will share a short spreadsheet before the legal redline cutoff.

DocuSign / next steps: I'll also share the DocuSign envelope link post-call for an interim NDA amendment if needed.

If that looks right I'll calendar the call and send the invite.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
